title: Quality Assurance, Quality Control and Laboratory Safety
summary: QC rules (Levey-Jennings, Westgard), pre-analytical error control and the basics of laboratory safety and regulations.
objectives: Distinguish quality assurance from quality control.
Apply basic Westgard rejection rules to a Levey-Jennings chart.
Identify major pre-analytical sources of error.

highYield: QC monitors the analytical process; QA covers the total testing process (pre-analytical, analytical, post-analytical).
Most lab errors occur in the pre-analytical phase (patient ID, specimen handling, transport).
quickReview.mnemonic: Westgard warning: 2 SD; rejection: 3 SD / 2-2s / R-4s.

deepStudy.introduction: A clinical laboratory produces results that drive medical decisions. Quality systems ensure each result is accurate, precise, timely and traceable — from specimen collection to reporting.

sections.heading: Quality control statistics
sections.body: Levey-Jennings charts plot control results over time with mean and SD lines. Westgard rules detect random and systematic error. When a rule is violated, the run is rejected, the cause investigated, controls repeated and only then patient results released.

sections.heading: Safety and regulations
sections.body: Standard precautions treat all specimens as infectious. Engineering controls (biosafety cabinets), PPE, sharps handling, chemical hygiene and spill response are mandatory. CLIA (and local equivalents like the Philippine FDA/DOH regulations) define personnel standards, QC and proficiency testing requirements.

deepStudy.clinicalSignificance: A single mislabeled specimen or out-of-control QC run can reach the patient — quality systems exist to prevent that.
deepStudy.labInterpretation: Proficiency testing (PT) compares your lab to peers; failures require documented investigation and corrective action.
examTraps: A 1_2s result alone does NOT reject a run — it is only a warning under Westgard.
Calibration and quality control are not the same: calibration sets the scale; QC verifies it.

memoryHooks.text: Pre-analytical errors = 'Pre' (before the machine even sees the sample).
